description: Offshore wind turbines must have a minimum intended capacity of at least 100 MW
context_quote: Applications must have a minimum intended capacity of at least 100MW.

description: Offshore wind turbines taller than 50 meters must undergo an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)
context_quote: More than 20 wind turbines taller than 50 m must undergo an EIA.

geographic_scope: Area within 500 meters of historic shipwreck (No. 551B)
context_quote: Furthermore, trenching activities are prohibited within 500 meters of the identified historic shipwreck (No. 551B) at all times.

context_quote: To protect sensitive habitats, vessel speeds for all project vessels shall not exceed 10 knots within the Block Island Sound Transit Lane.

description: Offshore wind farm projects in the UK between 1 MW and 100 MW are consented by the Marine Management Organisation (MMO), and projects over 100 MW are classified as Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects (NSIPs) and are processed by the Planning Inspectorate for England and Wales (PINS)
context_quote: In England and Wales, any offshore energy project between 1 and 100MW is consented by the Marine Management Organisation (MMO). Projects over 100MW are classified as a Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project (NSIP) and are processed by the Planning Inspectorate for England and Wales (PINS).

description: Offshore wind farm projects in Scotland are consented by the Marine Scotland Licensing Operations Team (MS-LOT) in a one-stop-shop procedure
context_quote: In Scotland, marine licenses are issued by the Marine Scotland Licensing Operations Team (MS-LOT) in a one-stop-shop procedure.

description: Offshore wind farm developers in Scotland must submit a Supply Chain Development Statement (SCDS) outlining the anticipated level and location of supply chain impact from their proposed project
context_quote: CES also requires developers to submit a Supply Chain Development Statement (SCDS), outlining the anticipated level and location of supply chain impact from their proposed project, broken down by project stage (development and consenting, construction, operation, and maintenance) and must be updated as project development progresses.

description: Offshore wind farm projects in Germany are regulated by the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency (BSH), a branch of the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWi), and the Federal Waterways and Shipping Administration (WSV)

context_quote: The rights to exploit energy from the wind in Danish territorial waters and in the EEZ are coordinated by DEA under the 2015 Danish Renewable Energy Promotion Act (RE Act), in co-operation with the Danish Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Danish Maritime Authority (DMA) and Danish Working Environment Authority (DWEA).

description: Offshore wind farm projects in Taiwan are regulated by the Bureau of Energy (BoE) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MoEA), the Industrial Development Bureau (IDB), Taiwan Power Company (TPC), and the Taiwanese Environmental Protection Administration (EPA)
context_quote: In Taiwan, the Bureau of Energy (BoE) of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MoEA) is responsible for setting policies for electricity businesses and issues, regulations, and electricity generation licenses. The Industrial Development Bureau (IDB), Taiwan Power Company (TPC) and the Taiwanese Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) are the entities that coordinate the permits for OWP.

description: Monopile foundations must not exceed 11 meters in diameter.
context_quote: Monopiles must be no larger than 11 m in diameter, representing the larger end of the monopile design.

description: No more than two monopile foundations may be installed per day.
context_quote: No more than two monopiles may be installed per day.

description: Pin pile foundations must not exceed 5 meters in diameter.
context_quote: Pin piles must be no larger than 5 m in diameter.

description: No more than three pin pile foundations may be installed per day.
context_quote: No more than three pin piles may be installed per day.

description: Impact pile driving is prohibited from January 1 through April 30.
context_quote: Impact pile driving must not occur January 1 through April 30.

description: Impact pile driving should be avoided in December, but may occur with prior NMFS approval.
context_quote: Impact pile driving must be avoided to the maximum extent practicable in December; however, it may occur if necessary to complete the project with prior approval by NMFS.

description: Impact pile driving may only occur during daylight hours in May, November, and (if approved) December.
context_quote: For the construction months of May and November (as well as December, if approval is granted by NMFS), impact pile driving must only be initiated during daylight hours, defined as no later than 1.5 hours prior to civil sunset and no earlier than 1 hour after civil sunrise, and would only be allowed to continue into darkness if stopping operations represents a risk to human health, safety, and/or pile stability.

description: Impact pile driving may occur during nighttime hours from June 1 to October 31, if an approved Alternative Monitoring Plan is in place.
context_quote: LOA Holder may initiate impact pile driving during hours of darkness only from June 1 to October 31, annually, in accordance with a NMFS-approved Alternative Monitoring Plan for Nighttime Pile Driving.

description: A soft-start protocol must be used for all impact pile driving, consisting of 4-6 strikes per minute at 10-20% of maximum hammer energy for at least 20 minutes.
context_quote: LOA Holder must utilize a soft-start protocol for each impact pile driving event of all foundations by performing four to six strikes per minute at 10 to 20 percent of the maximum hammer energy, for a minimum of 20 minutes.

description: Soft-start procedures must be used at the beginning of impact pile driving and after any cessation of 30 minutes or longer.
context_quote: Soft-start must occur at the beginning of impact driving and at any time following a cessation of impact pile driving of 30 minutes or longer.

description: At least two functional noise abatement systems that reduce noise levels by at least 10 dB must be used during all impact pile driving.
context_quote: LOA Holder must deploy at least two functional noise abatement systems that reduce noise levels to the modeled harassment isopleths, assuming 10-dB attenuation, during all impact pile driving.

description: Bubble curtains used as noise abatement systems must meet specific performance standards.
context_quote: Any bubble curtain(s) must distribute air bubbles using an air flow rate of at least 0.5 m^3 /(minute*m). The bubble curtain(s) must surround 100 percent of the piling perimeter throughout the full depth of the water column. The lowest bubble ring must be in contact with the seafloor for the full circumference of the ring, and the weights attached to the bottom ring must ensure 100-percent seafloor contact. No parts of the ring or other objects may prevent full seafloor contact with a bubble curtain ring.

description: NMFS-approved passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) systems must be used to detect marine mammals during impact pile driving.
context_quote: LOA Holder must utilize NMFS-approved PAM systems, as described in paragraph(c)(17) of this section. The PAM system components ( *i.e.,* acoustic buoys) must not be placed closer than 1 km to the pile being driven so that the activities do not mask the PAM system.

description: At least three on-duty protected species observers (PSOs) must be stationed on the pile driving platform, and two dedicated PSO vessels with at least three PSOs each must be used during impact pile driving.
context_quote: LOA Holder must utilize PSO(s) and PAM operator(s), as described in § 217.265(c). At least three on-duty PSOs must be on the pile driving platform. Additionally, two dedicated-PSO vessels must be used at least 60 minutes before, during, and 30 minutes after all pile driving, and each dedicated PSO vessel must have at least three PSOs on duty during these time periods.

description: Impact pile driving must be shut down if a marine mammal enters the respective shutdown zone, unless shutdown would result in imminent risk of injury, loss of life, or pile instability.
context_quote: If a marine mammal is detected (visually or acoustically) entering or within the respective shutdown zone after pile driving has begun, the PSO or PAM operator must call for a shutdown of pile driving and LOA Holder must stop pile driving immediately, unless shutdown is not practicable due to imminent risk of injury or loss of life to an individual or risk of damage to a vessel that creates risk of injury or loss of life for individuals, or the lead engineer determines there is pile refusal or pile instability.

description: A visual or acoustic detection of a North Atlantic right whale at any distance triggers a shutdown of impact pile driving.
context_quote: A visual observation or acoustic detection of a North Atlantic right whale at any distance triggers shutdown requirements under paragraph (c)(12) of this section.

description: Impact pile driving may not resume after a shutdown until the detected marine mammal has voluntarily left the clearance zone or a specific time period has elapsed with no further detections.
context_quote: If pile driving has been shut down due to the presence of a North Atlantic right whale, pile driving may not restart until the North Atlantic right whale has neither been visually or acoustically detected for 30 minutes; If pile driving has been shut down due to the presence of a marine mammal other than a North Atlantic right whale, pile driving must not restart until either the marine mammal(s) has voluntarily left the specific clearance zones and has been visually or acoustically confirmed beyond that clearance zone, or, when specific time periods have elapsed with no further sightings or acoustic detections have occurred. The specific time periods are 15 minutes for small odontocetes and pinnipeds, and 30 minutes for all other marine mammal species.

description: Up to 94 wind turbine generators within 102 potential positions
context_quote: The proposed Project would allow Sunrise Wind to construct, operate, maintain, and eventually decommission a wind energy facility with an operating capacity ranging between 924 megawatts (MW) and 1,034 MW in scale. The Project would include up to 94 wind turbine generators (WTGs) at 102 potential locations, one Offshore Converter Station (OCS-DC), offshore export cable routes, onshore cable landfall sites, onshore cable routes, and onshore substation locations.

description: WTG spacing of 1.15 miles (1 nautical mile, 1.8 kilometers) in an east-west/north-south grid
context_quote: Turbines would be sited in a uniform east-west/north-south grid with 1.15 by 1.15-mile (mi) (1 by 1-nautical mile [nm]; 1.85 by 1.85 kilometer [km]) spacing.

description: WTG rotor height up to 787 feet (240 meters) above mean sea level
context_quote: Turbines would be sited in a uniform east-west/north-south grid with 1.15 by 1.15-mile (mi) (1 by 1-nautical mile [nm]; 1.85 by 1.85 kilometer [km]) spacing. Sunrise Wind would maintain diagonal lanes between 0.7 and 0.9 mi (0.6 to 0.8 nm; 1.1 and 1.5 km) wide when micrositing foundations. Sunrise Wind would mount the WTGs on monopile foundations. The WTG foundations as proposed in the COP would be 39 ft (12 m) in diameter at the seabed and 23 ft (7 m) in diameter at the sea surface (Sunrise Wind 2022). A monopile foundation typically consists of a single steel tubular section, with several sections of rolled steel plate welded together. For a WTG monopile foundation, a Transition Piece (TP) may be fitted over the top of the monopile and secured via a bolted connection. Secondary structures on each WTG monopile foundation would include a boat landing or alternative means of safe access, a crane, and other ancillary components. The OCS-DC would be placed on an up to four-legged piled jacket foundation. A piled jacket foundation is formed of a steel lattice construction (comprising tubular steel members and welded joints) secured to the seafloor by means of hollow steel pin piles attached to the jacket. Schematic drawings and renderings of the conceptual monopile foundation with secondary structure after installation and the piled jacket foundations are included in COP Section 3.3.5 (Sunrise Wind 2022). When required, scour protection would be placed around foundations to stabilize the seabed near the foundations as well as the foundations themselves.

description: WTG monopile foundations up to 39 feet (12 meters) in diameter at the seabed
context_quote: Sunrise Wind would mount the WTGs on monopile foundations. The WTG foundations as proposed in the COP would be 39 ft (12 m) in diameter at the seabed and 23 ft (7 m) in diameter at the sea surface (Sunrise Wind 2022).

description: WTG monopile foundations up to 23 feet (7 meters) in diameter at the sea surface
context_quote: Sunrise Wind would mount the WTGs on monopile foundations. The WTG foundations as proposed in the COP would be 39 ft (12 m) in diameter at the seabed and 23 ft (7 m) in diameter at the sea surface (Sunrise Wind 2022).

description: OCS-DC foundation is a piled jacket structure with up to four legs
context_quote: The OCS-DC would be placed on an up to four-legged piled jacket foundation. A piled jacket foundation is formed of a steel lattice construction (comprising tubular steel members and welded joints) secured to the seafloor by means of hollow steel pin piles attached to the jacket.

description: Maximum total installed inter-array cable length of 180 miles (290 kilometers)
context_quote: The maximum total installed array cable length is 180 miles (289.7 km).

description: Offshore export cable length up to 106 miles (170 kilometers)
context_quote: The approximately 106 mi (170 km) SRWEC would occur within a surveyed corridor ranging in width from 1,312 to 2,625 ft (400 to 800 m), depending on water depth.

description: Offshore export cable target burial depth of 3 to 7 feet (1 to 2 meters)
context_quote: The SRWEC would consist of one cable bundle comprised of two cables. The cable would have a target burial depth of 3 to 7 ft (1 to 2 m) but would be dependent upon an assessment of seabed conditions, seabed mobility, the risk of interaction with external hazards, and a site-specific cable burial risk assessment.

description: Onshore transmission cable length up to 17.5 miles (28.2 kilometers)
context_quote: The interior transmission cable includes an OnCS-DC with a disturbance footprint of up to 7 ac (2.8 ha) and an operational footprint of 6 acres (2.4 ha). Benthic habitat types identified in the interior coastal component of the Project area include: - Tidal marsh (5 acres) - Summer flounder HAPC

description: Temporary pile-supported trestle extending approximately 240 feet (73 meters) offshore and 16 feet (4.9 meters) wide
context_quote: To allow for the transportation of equipment and materials from Long Island to the construction site on Fire Island, a temporary pile-supported pier would be constructed on the inshore side of Fire Island. The pier would extend approximately 240 feet (73 m) offshore and be approximately 16-feet (4.9-m) wide.

description: Up to 24 production piles for the temporary pile-supported trestle, either 14 x 14-inch (36.5 x 36.5 cm) H-shaped or 16-inch (40.6-cm) diameter round steel
context_quote: The precise pier design and type of piles have not yet been determined, but it is anticipated that up to 24 production piles would be used. Production piles would be either a 14 x 14-inch (36.5 x 36.5 cm) H-shaped pile or a 16-inch (40.6-cm) diameter round steel pile.

description: Up to 24 temporary piles for the temporary pile-supported trestle, either 14 x 14-inch (36.5 x 36.5 cm) H-shaped or 16-inch (40.6-cm) diameter round steel
context_quote: In addition, up to 24 temporary piles (of the same size as the production piles) may be used to support the installation of the production piles and may be installed and removed during construction activities.

description: Developers should evaluate multiple project design options for wind turbines, including type, number, size, location, and orientation, with a focus on avoiding and minimizing impacts to North Atlantic right whales (NARWs) and their habitat.
context_quote: Developers should evaluate multiple project design options such as the type, number, size (physical dimensions and power output), location, and orientation of wind turbines and offshore substations, with a focus on identifying design options that avoid and minimize impacts to NARWs and their habitat within and with adjacent projects; tradeoffs for other resources need to be evaluated during project planning.

description: Avoid installing wind turbine foundations during times of year when NARWs are most likely to be present in the lease areas and along vessel routes.
geographic_scope: Lease areas and vessel transit routes
context_quote: Project schedules should avoid installing foundations during the time of year when NARWs are most likely to occur in the lease areas and along vessel routes, including known areas of higher NARW density and persistence, and including, but not limited to, Nantucket Shoals, Cape Cod Bay, calving grounds, and designated NARW critical habitat.

description: Noise levels generated during wind turbine foundation installation (e.g., pile driving) must be reduced to the maximum extent practicable, with a goal of not exceeding NOAA Fisheries' Level A permanent threshold shift limits for low-frequency cetaceans at distances greater than 1,000 meters.
context_quote: Sound fields generated during impact pile driving should be reduced to the maximum extent practicable with a goal of not exceeding NOAA Fisheries' Level A permanent threshold shift (PTS) limits for low frequency cetaceans (LFC) at distances greater than 1,000 meters from each foundation.

description: Unexploded ordnance (UXO) must be addressed using the least impactful methods, prioritizing avoidance through micrositing, then low-order incineration over high-order detonation.
context_quote: The agencies are committed to working with Federal partners and lessees to develop and implement standard protocols for addressing unexploded ordinances, including implementation of best available technology to avoid or minimize exposure of NARWs and their sensitive habitats to in-situ disposal (low order incineration or high order detonation). If disposal is necessary, after demonstrating that avoidance through micrositing is not feasible, low order incineration is preferred over high order detonations.

description: Project vessels must maintain a speed of 10 knots or less when NARWs may be present or when visibility is poor.
context_quote: All vessels underway must not divert their course to approach any protected species. All vessels should have a dedicated lookout or PSO watching for NARWs at all times and slow to 10 knots or less at any time/location that NARWs may be present and at any time when visibility is poor.

description: Common eiders forage in water less than 10 meters (33 feet) deep
context_quote: Common eiders forage in water less than 10 m (33 feet) during the winter when diving over rocky substrate and kelp beds (Goudie et al . 2000; Guillemette et al ., 1993).

description: Scoters forage in water less than 20 meters (66 feet) deep, with a maximum diving depth of 25 meters (82 feet)
context_quote: Maximum diving depths of scoters are about 25 m (82 feet), although most birds probably forage in water less than 20 meters (66 feet) deep, particularly during the winter months (Vaitkus and Bubinas 2001; Bordage and Savard 1995).

description: The Met Buoy will consist of a floating platform with a NOMAD hull measuring 19.7 ft (6 m) long by 10.2 ft (3.1 m) wide, with a vertical profile of approximately 13.8 ft (4.2 m) from the sea surface to the top of the hull mast.
context_quote: The floating platform consists of the AXYS Navy Oceanographic Meteorological Automated Device (NOMAD) hull, mooring chain, and clump weight anchor (Figure 3-2). The NOMAD hull consists of marine grade aluminum and measures 19.7 ft (6 m) long by 10.2 ft (3.1 m) wide. The vertical profile of the Met Buoy including instrumentation will be approximately 13.8 ft (4.2 m) from the sea surface to the top of the hull mast.

description: The submerged portion of the Met Buoy hull will measure approximately 11.5 ft (3.5 m) below the sea surface from the water line to the bottom of the mooring yoke.
context_quote: The submerged portion of the hull would measure approximately 11.5 ft (3.5 m) below the sea surface from the water line to the bottom of the mooring yoke.

description: The Met Buoy will be moored to the seabed using a steel chain attached to 1 or 2 concrete clump weight anchors weighing a total of up to 10 metric tons.
context_quote: The hull would be moored to the seabed using a steel chain attached to 1 or 2 concrete clump weight anchors. The anchors would weigh a total of up to 10 metric tons and sit on the seabed for an area of up to 108 ft [2] (10 m [2] ).

description: The area of the anchor chain sweep associated with the long-term operation of the Met Buoy is anticipated to be approximately 12 acres (based on an anchor chain radius of approximately 410 ft (125 m) on the sea floor).
context_quote: The area of the anchor chain sweep associated with the long-term operation of the Met Buoy is anticipated to be approximately 12 acres (based on an anchor chain radius of approximately 410 ft (125 m) on the sea floor).

description: The Met Buoy will be equipped with a single or dual light detection and ranging (LIDAR) instrumentation package installed atop the hull, with each LIDAR unit approximately 3.3 ft (1 m) in height.
context_quote: A single or dual light detection and ranging (LIDAR) instrumentation package will be installed atop the hull. Each LIDAR unit is approximately 3.3 ft (1 m) in height.

description: The Met Buoy will be deployed for a 6-year operational life.
context_quote: The operational life of the Met Buoy is anticipated to be 6 years.

description: The Met Buoy will be located at or about 41° 05' 16" N 71° 13' 22" W within OCS Block 6965, Aliquot M of the Official Protraction Diagram Providence NK19-07.
context_quote: The Met Buoy will be deployed in federal waters of the Atlantic Ocean within OCS Block 6965, Aliquot M of the Official Protraction Diagram Providence NK19-07 (see Addendum A of North Lease, and Figure 1-1). The location of the Met Buoy is at or about 41° 05' 16" N and 71° 13' 22" W.

description: The Met Buoy installation, operation, and decommissioning activities will comply with the vessel-strike avoidance measures for marine mammals and sea turtles specified in the North Lease Stipulations 4.1.1.1 through 4.1.1.7.
context_quote: All whales, dolphins, and porpoises in the northeast region are federally protected by the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA) and many large whales in the area, as well as sea turtles, are further protected under the Endangered Species Act (ESA). The North Lease contains specific stipulations to minimize risk to marine mammals and sea turtles that must be followed.

description: Sightings of any injured or dead protected species (e.g., marine mammals or sea turtles) will be reported to the National Marine Fisheries Service Northeast Region's Stranding Hotline within 24 hours, regardless of whether the injury or death is caused by a vessel.
context_quote: The Lessee must ensure that sightings of any injured or dead protected species (e.g., marine mammals or sea turtles) are reported to the NMFS Northeast Region's Stranding Hotline (800- 900-3622 or current) within 24 hours of sighting, regardless of whether the injury or death is caused by a vessel.

description: Deepwater Wind will comply with BSEE NTL 2015-G03 regarding marine trash and debris prevention, including briefing all employees and contractors on marine trash and debris awareness and elimination.
context_quote: Deepwater Wind will comply with ensure that all employees and contractors are briefed on marine trash and debris awareness elimination, as required in Addendum C, Section 4.1.2 of the North Lease and as described in the BSEE NTL No. 2015-G03 which has superseded NTL 2012-G01.

description: Deepwater Wind will submit an Oil Spill Response Plan for the Met Buoy to the BSEE Oil Spill Response Division prior to deployment, demonstrating compliance with 30 CFR 254.22(a), 254.23(a) and 254.23(g)(1).

description: Deepwater Wind will conduct routine maintenance on the Met Buoy twice per year, using comparable or smaller vessels than the installation vessel.

description: Deepwater Wind will submit a decommissioning application to BOEM at least 6 months prior to decommissioning the Met Buoy, and will notify BOEM at least 60 days before commencing decommissioning activities.

description: After decommissioning the Met Buoy, Deepwater Wind will conduct a photographic or video bottom survey to provide evidence that the area has been cleared, as required by § 585.902(a)(2).
context_quote: Following decommissioning, Deepwater Wind will conduct a photographic or video bottom survey to provide objective evidence to BOEM that the area has been cleared as required in § 585.902(a)(2).
